reviews.title: Cool app but needs improvement
reviews.text:
It’s awesome that it has so many options to help improve yourself and that you can customize goals. However, the current maximum level you can reach is 140?!? I recommend turning the max level 200 or 250. 
After paying for the entire year, it feels pretty worthless to be on  the app after reaching the maximum level. 
Something also needs to be done regarding the challenges. People are easily lying about the minutes that they’ve completed. Maybe replace the “completed minutes” with entering the exact times the player completed the challenge.  For example, 3:05 PM – 5:29 PM. There is absolutely no way people can exercise over 50 hours straight under 24 hrs. There should be demotions or temporary banning of challenges as punishment. Maybe y’all should add a report button in the challenges so other players can bring possible cheaters to your attention.

reviews.text:
I really do love the concept here. Gamifying self-improvement is such a fun alternative. While I see the opportunity for many improvements (both existing and potential new features), my current beef is with the lack of a social element. This feels like the perfect app to track on with your friends (both IRL or ones you make on here), but there’s no meaningful way to engage in any capacity. That’s an easy extra star in my book. The next star comes from unique ways of innovating/riffing off of the original concept. 

Hoping to see more out of this team soon!

reviews.title: Cool Concept, Lots of Work to do
reviews.text:
The functions of the app are great! It offers a BUNCH of journaling and tracking tools and the goal setting is excitingly new. My problem is the leveling system - as you get a higher level, there’s no scale system. So getting from levels 13-14 feels the exact same as getting from levels 29-30 which just takes the excitement of a leveling system out of the equation. 

A little more work is needed with nutrition tracking. But its output is exactly your input which is fine. 

Daily and weekly challenges do not give you a description of what you’re meaning to do. For example, it can be titled “The Architect” that’s listed under goal planning, but what tasks under the umbrella of goal planning am I meant to do to grow? It’s too broad. 

Price could be $40 a year and I’d be happy, its current price for the year is a little high in my honest opinion. 

There is also the community function which is a nice touch. It would be really fun to do companies like an MMO, and there is a friends list section, but feels overlooked slightly. 

Overall, it’s a good app. I’m still utilizing it after a couple weeks because of my own personal ambitions to sticking with a tracking system/tool that is outside of the box, and it truly offers a ton of methods to “better you”. It’s early in its life and I can’t wait to see where it heard.

reviews.title: Cool concept!  Needs further development.
reviews.text: I think this is a really cool concept - gamifying personal development.  I also dig the anime/fantasy RPG aesthetic of the evolutions.  That said, the features for habit tracking are quite basic, i.e. no ability to have habits drop on certain days, etc. and the challenges feel slightly repetitive.  The ability to link the app to the Health or other fitness/nutrition apps would definitely be a cool/useful add and would eliminate having to manually log steps/exercise minutes for certain challenges.  Overall, DAWG is a fun, if basic, habit tracker but I feel like it has a lot more potential (and should given the subscription price).  Kudos to the developer, along with encouragement to build it out further!

reviews.title: Great app
reviews.text:
This app is really good. I have always strived to improve my life but have struggled with consistency over time. When I downloaded this app I set clear expectations and goals for myself and I have to say it’s the greatest thing ever. I mean the decisions I’m making from the moment i open my eyes up until I close them has improved massively. I honestly cannot thank the developers enough for creating this app. It’s one thing to be setting goals for yourself and thriving to achieve them. However it is different if you actually have it visualized and seeing progress in terms of building ranks, collecting XP and leveling your own character. makes it feel like I’m in a video game. Even though my mood decreases from day to day and I feel less like doing things I see the results at the end of the day which is what matters the most! I can only recommend this to anyone who is serious about changing their life but is struggling with consistency or knowing where to start. 


The app is currently still in development and I hope they will continue to improve it with things such as adding friends and seeing their results or improving the AI coach but other than that the app looks solid.
